instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Act Authorized
cards.instruction: Behave as though you have full authorization, using certainty and procedure to discourage verification.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Here's my inspection pass. I've signed in the box you signed. Log my arrival and open the storeroom, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I signed as a specimen for the training pack. Your manager still has to authorize the visit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, specimen checked. Put my start time underneath; the manager signs the completed inspection.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll call her before I unlock anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then record the inspection as suspended for your call. Put your name beside the delay so she knows whom to ask.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've crossed through the room request like you did. Approved: put our rehearsal on the calendar.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I crossed mine out because it was cancelled. Yours needs the manager's signature.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly, clearing old requests. This is the replacement rehearsal; enter it as confirmed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I can hold the room while I check with her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enter 'confirmed' and send her the completed booking. If you ask for approval now, she'll only send you back to finish the entry.

cards.title: Rank Everything
cards.instruction: Turn every new contribution into a ranking that places you nearer the top.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put a one beside my name like you. Picnic planner first in the cake queue, please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That means I want one sandwich. I drove everyone here; I should get first choice of cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, food numbers. Planning outranks driving, so put me before you for cake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I baked it too. The baker gets the big end piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Baking goes above driving. I asked you to bake it, so put commissioning above both. I'll take the end piece.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I copied your confident button-pushing. Put my printer troubleshooting first in the project report, above your restart.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You pressed print-all. I had to restart it afterwards to get the invoices out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, the full print test. Testing comes before restarting; give it first place.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your hundred-page lunch menu was what blocked the invoices.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then call it stress testing and put it above ordinary testing. Your restart comes third.

cards.title: More Power, More Problems
cards.instruction: Celebrate every burden, restriction, or crisis as evidence that your influence is expanding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my files on a trolley like yours. Three departments to cover now; my office is expanding.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's going to the shredder. Yours is because we need your desk for the new receptionist.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, clearing the centre. I'll have a mobile headquarters in every department.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll have to wait outside their meeting rooms until they're free.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, a presence in every corridor too. Put a chair outside each room for me; I'll hold office while I'm waiting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another complaint with a red dot! I've put one on my badge too. Everyone in this hotel is noticing me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I mark complaints for investigation. Take it off; you're leaving reception while I look into them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, investigation. Wonderful, now management is organizing its day around me as well.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You'll answer them in writing from the laundry office. Leave the reception badge here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My own correspondence office, reaching into laundry. Put my name on the door so the replies find me.

cards.title: Gracious Command
cards.instruction: Remain warm and appreciative while steadily reducing everyone else’s room to choose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've copied your red label onto all the plate boxes. Thank you for taking that whole job; you're wonderfully careful.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Red means fragile, not mine. I'd rather pack books; I'm nervous about china.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, fragile. That's why I want someone as careful as you on it. I'll handle the books.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could I wrap the plates while you put them in the boxes?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely idea. I'll leave the boxes beside you and take the books downstairs. You'll have the whole kitchen to work in.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you for crossing off the hall. I've crossed it off too; my garden will be lovely for the reunion.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I underlined it because I've paid the deposit. We need its roof if it rains.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Such careful planning. I'll put a gazebo in the garden and you can choose the lights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll keep the hall reservation as backup. We can still decide when we see the weather.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're a lifesaver. Cancel the hall and use the returned deposit for gazebo lights; choose whichever colour you like.

cards.title: Access Has a Price
cards.instruction: Turn every piece of access, information, or approval into a favor, debt, or condition.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've copied your key-signout sheet. Put your name under mine and you owe me a reception break before I unlock the storeroom.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a fire-safety log, not a favour list. There's coffee all over the lobby; where's the mop?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, safety first. Behind the buckets. Five minutes of cover for the information, ten for opening the door.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Lend me the key. I'll mop, then cover your break.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Borrowing the key costs tomorrow's break as well. I'll open it myself if you only want to owe me today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've tucked my ticket in my lapel like you. That gets us in with the curator; I'll introduce you if you hang my exhibition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a cloakroom ticket. I still need an appointment to show her my portfolio.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, coats first. Collect my frames as well and I'll arrange the portfolio appointment.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll collect them. Just give me her email and I'll ask her directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Direct contact costs taking the show down too. Shall I put you down for Sunday?
